qa_pairs.instruction: What is the primary purpose of using style sheets in the Delimited Text driver for Identity Manager?
qa_pairs.output: In the Delimited Text driver, style sheets are used to configure data synchronization and do most of the work in managing shared data. The driver passes text-based files largely unchanged to the style sheets, which perform the actual data transformation. Style sheets allow the Delimited Text driver to work with almost any text-based file that contains predictably repeatable patterns, making the driver flexible and customizable.

qa_pairs.instruction: What is the <delimited-text> XML element in the Delimited Text driver?
qa_pairs.output: The <delimited-text> XML element is the basis for data exchange in the Delimited Text driver. It serves as a structured XML representation of the data from text files. This element contains <record> elements, each with multiple <field> elements that have 'name' attributes and values. Style sheets convert text file contents into <delimited-text> elements for processing by Identity Manager.

qa_pairs.instruction: Why does the Delimited Text driver rely heavily on style sheets rather than built-in parsing?
qa_pairs.output: The Delimited Text driver relies heavily on style sheets because the driver is designed to be as flexible as possible. By passing text-based files largely unchanged to style sheets and letting the style sheets do most of the work, you can write new style sheets to allow the driver to work with almost any text-based file that contains predictably repeatable patterns. This design approach maximizes flexibility without requiring changes to the driver itself.

qa_pairs.instruction: How do you design a Publisher channel in the Delimited Text driver to read information from a text file?
qa_pairs.output: To design a Publisher channel in the Delimited Text driver that reads information from a text file, create an Input Transform style sheet that receives the contents of the file and converts it into a <delimited-text> XML element. The style sheet transforms the raw text data into the structured <delimited-text> format with <record> and <field> elements that Identity Manager can process.

qa_pairs.instruction: What types of style sheets are available in the example configuration for the Delimited Text driver?
qa_pairs.output: In the Delimited Text driver's example configuration, the following style sheet types are available: Input Transform style sheets, Output Transform style sheets, and Event Transformation style sheets. These sample style sheets can be used as a starting point when creating the driver using the example configuration.

qa_pairs.instruction: Provide an example of a properly structured <delimited-text> XML element for the Delimited Text driver with two records containing FirstName, LastName, and Phone fields.
qa_pairs.output:
```xml
<delimited-text>
     <record>
          <field name="FirstName">John</field>
          <field name="LastName">Maxfield</field>
          <field name="Phone">555-1212</field>
     </record>
     <record>
          <field name="FirstName">Sarah</field>
          <field name="LastName">Lopez</field>
          <field name="Phone">555-3434</field>
     </record>
</delimited-text>
```

qa_pairs.instruction: Can the Delimited Text driver work with file formats other than comma-separated values?
qa_pairs.output: Yes, the Delimited Text driver can work with file formats other than comma-separated values. Although the example configuration uses comma-separated value files, the driver can be used in many ways and is designed to be as flexible as possible. You can write new style sheets to allow the driver to work with almost any text-based file that contains predictably repeatable patterns.

qa_pairs.instruction: Where can you find detailed information and examples for writing style sheets to handle different document types in the Delimited Text driver?
qa_pairs.output: For detailed information on writing style sheets to handle other document types in the Delimited Text driver, refer to the sample style sheets that come with the driver. If you create the driver using the example configuration, you can use the included Input Transform, Output Transform, and Event Transformation style sheets as a starting point for customization.

qa_pairs.instruction: Summarize the key concepts for configuring data synchronization using style sheets in the Delimited Text driver.
qa_pairs.output: The Delimited Text driver uses style sheets as the primary mechanism for managing data synchronization. The driver passes text-based files largely unchanged to style sheets, which perform the actual transformation work. The basis for data exchange is the <delimited-text> XML element containing <record> and <field> elements. While the example configuration uses CSV files, the driver is highly flexible and can work with almost any text-based file with predictable patterns by writing custom style sheets. Sample style sheets (Input Transform, Output Transform, and Event Transformation) are provided with the example configuration as starting points for customization.
